title: 16-week-trajectory-brief-and-ask-scripts
content:
Purpose: compact 16-week trajectory map for my manager sync + two concise ask scripts. This is a living scratchpad — keep it short in the meeting, bring depth when asked.

High level objective (16 weeks): Own and land a lightweight calibration playbook for talent review that reduces manual prep time for managers by 40% and increases calibration signal fidelity (quantified) across two teams. Secondary objective: pilot a development micro-grant (4x $2k awards) to run skills experiments with measurable outcomes.

Why this matters (one-liner): Remove friction from performance calibration and create a repeatable, measurable channel to surface high-potential contributors across product orgs.

Success metrics (how I'll measure):
- Reduction in average manager prep time (baseline: 3.5 hrs) to <= 2 hrs for calibration cycles (measured via self-report + time-tracking sample)
- Calibration precision: increase fraction of calibration items with consensus across raters from 62% -> >=78%
- Deliverable adoption: two teams adopt the playbook end-to-end in cycle N+1
- Micro-grant outcomes: 3/4 experiments demonstrate a defined improvement (example: reduce PR review lag by >=10% or increase experiment velocity)

Quarter roadmap (high level milestones):
Weeks 1-2: Audit existing artifacts (templates, rubrics, evaluation tickets). Quick interviews with 6 managers (15–20m).
Weeks 3-6: Draft playbook v0: rubric + one-page manager guide + calibration checklist; 1 pilot team onboarding.
Weeks 7-10: Run pilot calibration session + collect signals; iterate.
Weeks 11-13: Micro-grant launch + admin playbook for running grants. 2nd team trial.
Weeks 14-16: Incorporate feedback, finalize playbook, handoff to people-ops enablement, prepare adoption package.

Primary risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Managers too busy to pilot -> Mitigation: reduce ask to 20m micro-calibration and offer 1:1 admin support for the first run.
- Risk: Signal noise from small sample -> Mitigation: combine qualitative notes with structured anchors and run two short pilots.
- Risk: Budget pushback on micro-grants -> Mitigation: position grants as low-cost experiments with clear ROI and tie to learnings + shareable artifacts.

Compact evidence bank (short snippets I can read out):
- Jan 2025: ran pilot rubric for Eng infra hiring loop; reduced calibration prep from ~3h to ~1.5h for two managers (links: JIRA-OPS-987, PR#412).
- Nov 2024: coordinated cross-team talent signal experiment; flagged 5 high-potential contributors who later received stretch assignments.
- Dec 2024: built one-page rubric that managers rated as "actionable" in 4/5 feedback notes.

Manager ask scripts (choose tone based on context)
1) Direct ask (time-constrained sync, 5 minutes):
- "Quick one: I'm piloting a 16-week playbook to reduce calibration prep and surface hidden talent. I'd like your support to run a 20-minute micro-calibration with your eng team in March and your feedback on the one-pager afterward. If you can commit one slot, I will handle scheduling and notes. Is that OK?"
Possible manager replies and my follow-ups:
- If yes: "Great — I’ll send a calendar invite and a 3-line prep note. I’ll also include a quick feedback form so it’s a 2-min effort post-session."
- If hesitant: "I can do an admin-led run where I capture notes and share the highlights — no prep from you besides a 20-min slot. Should I plan for that?"

2) Stretch ask (if manager is engaged, 10 minutes):
- "I’d like to propose a small micro-grant pilot to help contributors run skills experiments (4 x $2k). The ask: one sponsor per grant from willing managers and a 30-min check-in cadence. The upside is rapid, measurable improvement and a template we can scale. Can I count on you to sponsor or nominate someone?"
Objections + counters:
- Budget: "I’ll scope the pilot as low-cost and deliver a post-pilot ROI memo — we can pause after one cohort if signals aren’t strong."
- Time: "Sponsors only need to commit 30 minutes total over the pilot and check-ins can be grouped."

Prep checklist for the meeting (what I bring):
- One-pager playbook (PDF) + 1-slide adoption ask
- 20-min runbook (facilitator script)
- Evidence snippets (3 bullets) + link to JIRA pilot tickets
- Clear CTA: sign up one slot OR nominate a sponsor

Who to loop in if manager asks for context: 
- Marcus Chen (enablement) — facilitator support
- Evelyn Park (data) — measurement plan and dashboard

Follow-ups after commit (template):
- Send calendar + 3-line prep note
- Collect post-session quick feedback (2 Qs, <2 mins)
- Share top 3 themes and a 1-page summary within 5 business days

Notes-to-self: keep language non-evaluative and outcome-focused. Lead with "how this reduces friction for you" not with "process changes." When sharing evidence, keep it lightweight: one concrete metric, one quote, one next step.

Open items to resolve before pilot:
- Finalize consent language for evidence collection (talk to legal?) -> pinged Legal on 2025-02-14 (no reply yet).
- Template for micro-grant application (one page) -> draft due week 6.
- Quick dashboard: ask Evelyn for a sample visualization of prep-time reduction by week -> create mock by week 4.

Quick version for slack invite (copy/paste):
"Running a 20-min micro-calibration pilot to reduce manager prep and improve signal fidelity. Looking for one slot from your team in March. I’ll handle facilitation + notes. Reply with preferred weekdays or drop an available 20-min slot and I’ll send invite"

End notes: keep this doc <=1 page for read during sync. Expand evidence bank in a separate doc only if asked. After each pilot, drop a one-line learning into #people-ops-pilots so momentum is visible.
